vocabulary.definition: relating to the structure and development of the universe on a large scale
vocabulary.example: The cosmological horizon marks the point beyond which objects are moving away from us faster than the speed of light.

vocabulary.definition: the rapid expansion of the universe in the early stages of its existence
vocabulary.example: During cosmic inflation, the universe grew from a tiny bubble to trillions of kilometers in a fraction of a second.

vocabulary.definition: able to be seen or noticed
vocabulary.example: The observable universe consists of galaxies and structures that we can detect with our current technology.

vocabulary.definition: related to the force of gravity or the influence of gravity
vocabulary.example: Objects in the universe form groups of galaxies by being gravitationally attracted to each other.

vocabulary.definition: a particular area of activity, influence, or expertise
vocabulary.example: A super advanced civilization could have a sphere of influence that extends to thousands of galaxies.

vocabulary.definition: open and honest, without hidden agendas
vocabulary.example: Kurzgesagt aims to be transparent by providing detailed sources and fact-checking processes in their videos.
